faq.q: What is an Exchange Traded Fund (ETF)?
faq.a: An ETF is a type of investment fund that holds assets like stocks, bonds, or commodities, and trades on stock exchanges like regular shares. It offers diversification and can be bought or sold throughout the trading day.

faq.q: What is tracking error in an ETF?
faq.a: Tracking error is the difference between an ETF's performance and the performance of its underlying benchmark index. A lower tracking error indicates that the ETF is more accurately replicating its index.

faq.q: How does the new SEBI framework improve ETF liquidity?
faq.a: The new framework likely includes stricter obligations for market makers, requiring them to provide continuous quotes and maintain tighter bid-ask spreads, thereby enhancing the ETF's trading liquidity.

faq.q: Will the new framework impact ETF expense ratios?
faq.a: While the primary goal is not to directly reduce expense ratios, improved operational efficiency and increased competition due to the framework *could* indirectly lead to more competitive expense ratios over time.

faq.q: Is this framework beneficial for all types of investors?
faq.a: Yes, it benefits both long-term investors through reduced tracking error and more accurate index replication, and short-term traders through tighter bid-ask spreads and improved liquidity.

faq.q: Where can I find official information on SEBI's new ETF framework?
faq.a: Official notifications and circulars regarding the new framework are published on the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) website ([https://sebi.gov.in](https://sebi.gov.in)).
